title: Sequence length warmup schedule not ablated
description: The schedule for sequence length warmup during DNA pretraining was not tuned, and the authors note they never experimented with turning it off, so its necessity is unconfirmed.
canonical_description: sequence length warmup schedule not ablated in pre-training experiments

evidence.anchor: we never experimented with turning off sequence length warmup
evidence.quote: We also note that the schedule was not tuned, and we never experimented with turning off sequence length warmup for these pretraining experiments.

verdict.reasoning: No candidate papers were deep-read, so there is no evidence the gap has been addressed.

ranking.feasibility_reasoning: Highly tractable: focused ablation of a single hyperparameter (warmup schedule) with clear experimental design — just vary or remove the schedule while keeping everything else fixed. Data is abundant and public. Evaluation metrics (perplexity, downstream benchmarks) are standard and well-defined. No methodological breakthrough needed. The main limiting factor is compute: full pre-training runs are expensive, but the ablation can likely be performed with a smaller proxy model or shorter training, keeping it within reach of a small team with modest GPU resources. Score slightly below 1.0 because compute cost is nontrivial and the effect might be noisy at smaller scales, but the gap is clearly well-scoped and addressable.
